description: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads) so the smaller model gets more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Set ASPECT_RATIO to 80 so the depth-8 model is wider (dim 640, 5 heads of dim 128).
Make the Muon momentum ramp faster (100 steps instead of 300) and peak at 0.97 during the stable phase, then decay to 0.95 over the warmdown.
Replace the relu^2 MLP with a SwiGLU MLP (hidden = 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64, which keeps parameters equal).
Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 so grad accumulation halves and the model gets about twice as many optimizer steps in 300 s.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 3% of the time budget.
Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine-shaped decay over the same WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget.

If the visible diff is really the whole change, the candidate is the same as the incumbent. The 1.1131 vs 1.1145 gap would then be run-to-run noise, not a real gain.

There is only 1 candidate run against 16 incumbent runs, and z = 0.242 is far below any usual significance threshold. The provisional reject decision fits the numbers. No claim contradicts them, but no improvement is shown either.
I can't recompute z because the incumbent's standard deviation isn't given. The reported z = 0.242 with a mean gap of 0.0014 implies a standard deviation of about 0.0058, but I can't check that.
No veto: the visible diff shows no tampering and no bug. The real edit should be supplied and reviewed again before this candidate is accepted.

Keep an EMA of all parameters (decay 0.99, since a 0.999 window is longer than the ~hundreds of steps in a 300 s run), updated each optimizer step with _foreach_lerp_, and copy it into the model just before the final eval.

issues: (1) Nothing affects measurement. The diff changes only WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3, a schedule hyperparameter. It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call or the summary printing, and the harness raised no integrity flags.
(2) No bugs. With WARMUP_RATIO 0.0 and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.3, the two fractions add up to less than 1, so the LR schedule is still valid and the result means something.

(3) The numbers agree with each other. The candidate's 1.1141 is 0.0004 lower (better) than the incumbent mean of 1.1145, and the positive z points the same way. I can't check the exact z = 0.070 because the incumbent's standard deviation isn't given. If z is the gap divided by the incumbent's spread, that spread would be about 0.0057.
There is only one candidate run, and the gain is well inside run-to-run noise, so the provisional reject is justified. A replicate would be needed before anyone could claim an improvement.

description: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3 so more of the training time is spent at full learning rate.
Add a z-loss term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the loss in GPT.forward only when the model is in training mode, so the eval path is unchanged.
Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 for the token and value embedding Adam groups.
Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSSSSL" so only the last layer uses full attention, making attention cheaper.
